name: bill-splitter
title: Bill splitter
description: Split the bill at the table: equally or by item, with a tip and an optional round-up, in whole cents so the shares always add up to the bill.
docs: Pass the bill as total in minor units (9640 is 96.40) and people as a count or as names. With items (name, amount and sharedBy, the positions of the people who had it) the bill can also be split by item: a line with no names is shared by everyone, and whatever the lines do not cover (a service charge, a discount) is shared in proportion to what each person had and shown as its own row. tipPercent starts the tip and tipOptions sets the choices. The count of people, the sharedBy of each line and tipPercent are starting values: after that the people at the table change them on the screen, and a later change of the prop does not undo that (give the component a new key to start over). Every sum is done in whole minor units and the odd cent goes to the first people in line, so the shares always add up to the bill; in an equal split the screen names who pays the cent more. defaultRoundUp lifts every share to a whole unit and shows the difference as its own line. onPay receives each share (subtotal, tip, rounding and total) when its button is pressed: return a promise to show it is working, reject to keep the share unpaid and say so. Once someone has paid, the split is fixed. Pass paid (positions) to control who has paid. Without onPay the splitter is a calculator with no buttons. Someone without a name is Guest 1, Guest 2 and so on (labels.guest). The chips under a dish and the sentence about the odd cent use short names: the first name, the first name with the initial of the last name ('Anna V.') when two first names collide, and a guest's whole label, so two chips never read the same. In a wide card up to four people sit beside the dish on one line; with more they stay under it and wrap. The result is a polite status; labels holds every word.
